text:
Predicates:
Adores(x, y) ::: x adores y.
DesignStyle(x, y) ::: x is a design style of y.
InterestingGeometries(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
Design(x, y) ::: x is a design by y.
Maks(x) ::: x is Max.
ZahaHadid(x) ::: x is Zaha Hadid.
KellyWearstler(x) ::: x is Kelly Wearstler.
Style(x, y) ::: x is a style of y.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Adores(x, y) ∧ DesignStyle(y, z) ∧ ZahaHadid(z) → InterestingGeometries(y)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x ∀y (Adores(x, y) ∧ DesignStyle(y, w) ∧ Brutalist(w) → ¬InterestingGeometries(y)) ::: No brutalist buildings that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (Adores(x, y) ∧ DesignStyle(y, z) → (ZahaHadid(z) ∨ KellyWearstler(z))) ::: Every style that Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's or Kelly Wearstler's.
∀x (Adores(x, y) ∧ DesignStyle(y, KellyWearstler) ∧ KellyWearstler(y) → Evocative(y)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler's styles that Max adores are evocative.
∀x (Adores(x, y) ∧ DesignStyle(y, KellyWearstler) ∧ KellyWearstler(y) → Dreamy(y)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler's styles that Max adores are dreamy.
∀x (Design(x, y) ∧ Adores(y, x) ∧ HasInterestingGeometries(x) → (Brutalist(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a design by Max that he adores has interesting geometries, then the design is a brutalist building and evocative.

Conclusion:
∃x (Design(x, maks) ∧ Brutalist(x)) ::: A design by Max is a brutalist building.
